decision: P04-001 Ezek.20.1-Ezek.20.26 HOLDS as one row. Test (c) does not bind at 20:3: the verse-final utterance formula there is the SIGNATURE OF AN OATH (חַי אָ֨נִי֙ אִם אִדָּרֵ֣שׁ לָכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה — the only one of the fourteen oath-plus-signature verses in the book whose signature is verse-final), which the strategy classes as an emphatic sub-onset device of a verdict paragraph and never a row close; the utterance formula is oracle-final only when a fresh onset follows, and 20:4 (הֲתִשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֹתָ֔ם הֲתִשְׁפּ֖וֹט בֶּן אָדָ֑ם) carries no word-event, no messenger formula, no 'and you, son of man', no 'therefore' and no mark — a bare 'son of man' address, which is onset corroboration and never an onset alone. A cut would make a 3-verse frame row (dateline, word-event, refusal) and open 20:4-26 on a question; the strategy's licensed internal seams of the history disputation are 20:27, 20:30, 20:39 only, all 'therefore … thus says' after a refrain, and the row already applies them. The row's own rationale already discloses the 20:3 oath and signature as paragraph-internal; it gains the rejected (c) cut as a named alternative.
reason: Bytes: Ezek.20.3 ends נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה with חַי אָ֨נִי֙ in the same verse (sweep: 16 verses carry חי אני, 14 with the signature in the same verse, exactly one — 20:3 — with the signature verse-final); Ezek.20.4 skeleton התשפט אתם התשפוט בן אדם את תועבת אבותם הודיעם; Ezek.20.5 messenger formula opens the recital; marks in ch 20: samekh after 20:1 and 20:26, pe after 20:44; Ezek.20.26 close לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵֽדְע֔וּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה + samekh; Ezek.20.27 לָכֵ֞ן ... כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר. WEB 20:3-4 read the same way (the oath closes the refusal; 20:4 is a question). §2a: oath = sub-onset, never a row onset; utterance mid-unit = paragraph-final unless a fresh onset follows.

decision: Both rows HOLD; no messenger formula inside either carries an addressee change. P01-009 Ezek.5.1-Ezek.5.17: the formulae at 5:5 (זֹ֚את יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם, the city in the third person), 5:7 (לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר, 2mp — הֲמָנְכֶם֙, סְבִיבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֔ם, הֲלַכְתֶּ֔ם) and 5:8 (לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ ... הִנְנִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ, 2fs) address ONE party — Jerusalem and the people in her — under the interpretation of the hair sign; the 2mp/2fs alternation continues inside the verdict itself (5:16 2mp, 5:17 both), so grammatical person is not an addressee change of the §2d.6 kind (Ammon → Moab; shepherds → flock; mountains → land). No refrain stands before 5:7 or 5:8 (the samekh after 5:6 and 5:7 are marks alone), the 'therefore' here follows an indictment, not a refrain, and the verdict is bound to the act byte-for-byte: 5:12 ends with the identical clause 5:2 ends with (וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם, byte tier; sweep: 3 verses book-wide — 5:2, 5:12, 12:14). G2 already held the 5:5 seam; this extends it to 5:7 and 5:8. P07-006 Ezek.31.1-Ezek.31.18: 31:10 (לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ ... יַ֕עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּבַ֖הְתָּ) and 31:15 (כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר ... בְּי֨וֹם רִדְתּ֤וֹ שְׁא֨וֹלָה֙) keep the cedar/Pharaoh figure of 31:2 throughout, 31:18 returns to Pharaoh in the second person and closes on the utterance formula + samekh; G8 already ratified the chapter as one row and the row's rationale already says both formulae change no addressee. decision: The 143 entries are split into two classes and the harmful one is normalised. HARMFUL — multi-ref entries ('oshb:Ezek.10.20 and oshb:Ezek.10.22 (…)', 'oshb:Ezek.14.14, oshb:Ezek.14.16, oshb:Ezek.14.18, oshb:Ezek.14.20 (…)', 'oshb:Ezek.12.15 and oshb:Ezek.12.16 (…)', 'oshb:Ezek.13.21 and oshb:Ezek.13.23 (…)' and any like them): citation_sweep parses only the FIRST ref of an entry (REF_RE binds the rest into the tail), so the second and later refs are neither range-guarded nor used as the key for the tail's mark/paseq/K/Q claims — a claim about the second verse is checked at the first verse. These are normalised by a deterministic, lossless split into one entry per ref, each carrying the original tail verbatim, ordered as CWO-EZ-11 and executed by the orchestrator AFTER the author wave is applied (the wave rewrites many refs) and BEFORE the suite re-run; any HARD problem the split surfaces goes to a targeted fix-up execution for that part under a fresh execution id. COSMETIC — a single ref with words before its parenthesis ('oshb:Ezek.8.1 carries paseq (1x, count-only, …)', 'oshb:Ezek.22.1 word-event formula (strict, 39-list)'): the tools read these correctly; the same sweep re-shapes them losslessly to ref + ' (' + tail + ')' so every entry matches the strict R1 shape, with a per-row manifest. AUTHOR-CLASS — the thirteen p06 entries of the form 'web:Ezek.C.V = "…"' embed WEB text in a ref: p06's author execution converts each to 'web:Ezek.C.V (onset text quoted in prose)' and, where the quotation is wanted, carries it in prose as curly-quoted WEB text with the inline web: ref (convention C3); this is an extra order to p06.
